F01.proposition: The Royal College of Art has announced the establishment of a new School of Communication & Design.
F01.support_span: The Royal College of Art, the world’s number one art and design university, has announced the establishment of a new School of Communication & Design .

F02.proposition: The new School brings communication and design disciplines together within a single, unified academic entity.
F02.support_span: The new School brings together communication and design disciplines within a single, unified academic entity.

F03.proposition: The new School will operate alongside the RCA's existing School of Architecture and School of Arts & Humanities, streamlining the university's academic framework into a three-School structure.
F03.support_span: It will operate alongside the RCA’s existing School of Architecture and School of Arts & Humanities, streamlining the university's academic framework into a three-School structure.

F04.proposition: The RCA's announcement of the new School is dated 1 September 2026.

F06.proposition: The RCA describes the move as reflecting the increasingly interconnected nature of communication and design practices.
F06.support_span: The strategic move reflects the increasingly interconnected nature of communication and design practices.

F07.proposition: The RCA says the School will provide increased opportunities for interdisciplinary working, shared learning and cross-School engagement, with collaboration supported through teaching, research and creative practice.
F07.support_span: The School will provide increased opportunities for interdisciplinary working, shared learning and cross-School engagement with collaboration actively supported through teaching, research and creative practice.

F08.proposition: The RCA states the School will bring together material intelligence, making, emerging technologies and critical enquiry to address complex challenges facing society, culture and industry.
F08.support_span: bringing together material intelligence, making, emerging technologies and critical enquiry to address the complex challenges facing society, culture and industry.

F09.proposition: The RCA describes the establishment of the School as a major step in its academic vision to champion progressive, collaborative education.
F09.support_span: The establishment of the School of Communication & Design marks a major step in the RCA’s academic vision to champion progressive, collaborative education fit for the future of global industry and culture.

F10.proposition: The RCA announcement lists fifteen programmes to be delivered from the new School, including Intelligent Mobility (MA) and Service Design (MA).
F10.support_span: Programmes which will be delivered from the new School of Communication & Design will be: Animation (MA) , Communication (MFA) , Communication (MPhil/PhD) , Creative Education (MEd) , Design (PGR) , Design Futures (MDes) , Design Products (MA) , Digital Direction (MA) , Fashion (MA) , Information Experience Design (MA) , Innovation Design Engineering (MA/MSc) , Intelligent Mobility (MA) , Service Design (MA) , Textiles (MA) , and Visual Communication (MA) .

F11.proposition: The programme list published by Creative Boom omits Intelligent Mobility (MA) and Service Design (MA), and gives Communication as MFA/PGR rather than as separate MFA and MPhil/PhD entries.
F11.support_span: Programmes which will be delivered from the new School of Communication & Design will be: Animation (MA), Communication (MFA/PGR), Creative Education (MEd), Design (PGR), Design Futures (MDes), Design Products (MA), Digital Direction (MA), Fashion (MA), Information Experience Design (MA), Innovation Design Engineering MA/MSc, Textiles (MA), and Visual Communication (MA).

F26.proposition: Creative Boom writes that today it does not matter whether a practitioner's title is graphic designer, product designer or motion designer, because they are expected to do a bit of everything as the industry demands.
